query: Which attention scope and edge-construction strategies (local k-nearest, learned edges, fully-connected) yield the best trade-off between coordination and scalability in graph critics?

response.query: Which attention scope and edge-construction strategies (local k-nearest, learned edges, fully-connected) yield the best trade-off between coordination and scalability in graph critics?
response.answer: Learned edges yield the best trade-off between coordination and scalability in graph critics. They balance complexity and performance effectively. Fully-connected approaches are scalable but lack coordination efficiency. Local k-nearest is less scalable due to high computational costs.
